functionDeclarations.description:
Execute a Python script in a sandboxed environment for automation and complex operations.

**Two modes:**
• **Inline**: Pass code via `script` parameter
• **Stored**: Pass `name` to run a saved script from the library (see list_scripts)

**IMPORTANT: Before writing scripts, please read the scripting documentation first!**
Use the command: `get_user_documentation_content filename='scripting.md'`

**Tool Documentation:**
To see available tools and their parameters, ask: 'Show me the available tools'

**Execution Environment:**
• Timeout: 10 minutes maximum execution time (to allow for external API calls)
• Sandboxed: No file system or network access
• Deterministic: No random numbers or current time

**Sandbox Limitations:**
The Monty scripting engine runs a sandboxed Python subset with these restrictions:
• No class definitions (can't use `class` keyword)
• No generators or yield statements
• No match/case statements
• No context managers or with statements
• No del statement
• No dict unpacking in literals ({**d1, **d2} not supported)
• No str.format() method (use f-strings instead)
• No map/filter functions (use list comprehensions instead)
• Decorators are buggy (avoid using them)
• Exceptions only accept 0 or 1 string arguments
• No imports except heavily sandboxed os, sys, typing, pathlib modules
• Resource limits: 256MB memory, 100 recursion depth
• However: try/except, while loops, float(), set(), frozenset() ARE supported

**Built-in Functions:**
• Type conversions: bool(), int(), str(), list(), tuple(), dict()
• Collections: len(), range(), sorted(), reversed(), enumerate(), zip()
• Logic: all(), any(), max(), min()
• Object inspection: type(), dir(), getattr(), hasattr()
• Control: print(), fail() - print() output is captured and returned to you under a '--- Script Output ---' section (use it to surface intermediate values without returning them)
• JSON: json_encode(value), json_decode(value)
• Base64: base64_encode(data), base64_decode(data) -> str, base64_decode_bytes(data) -> bytes
• LLM Wake: wake_llm(context, include_event=True) - Request LLM attention with context (string or dict)
• LLM: llm(prompt), llm_json(prompt) - One-shot LLM calls for summarisation and data extraction

**Family Assistant Tools:**
All enabled tools are available as functions. Call them directly:
• add_or_update_note(title='...', content='...')
• search_notes(query='...')
• send_email(to='...', subject='...', body='...')

**Note**: Tools return structured data (dicts, lists) directly. You can use results
immediately without parsing. `json_decode()` is safe to call on any value - it passes
through dicts, lists, numbers, and booleans unchanged, and only parses strings:
```python
notes = search_notes(query='TODO')  # Returns a list directly
for note in notes:
    print(note['title'])
```

**Tools API Functions:**
• tools_list() - List all available tools with descriptions
• tools_get(name) - Get detailed info about a specific tool
• tools_execute(name, **kwargs) - Execute a tool by name

**LLM API Functions:**
• llm(prompt, system=None, model=None) - One-shot LLM call, returns text
• llm_json(prompt, schema=None, system=None, model=None) - One-shot LLM call, returns parsed JSON
Default model: gemini-3.6-flash. Useful for summarisation, data extraction, classification.

**Attachment API Functions:**
• attachment_get(attachment_id) - Get attachment metadata by ID
• attachment_create(content, filename, description, mime_type) - Create new attachment
Note: attachment_list() and attachment_send() are not available.
Scripts must receive attachment IDs from LLM context, tool results, or parameters.

**Returning Attachments:**
Attachments created by tools or attachment_create() are represented as dictionaries
with metadata: {"id": uuid, "filename": str, "mime_type": str, "size": int, "description": str}
Return these dicts to make attachments visible to the LLM:

```python
# Single attachment - last expression is returned
data = attachment_create(content="data", filename="data.txt", mime_type="text/plain")
data  # Dict with attachment info, automatically sent to LLM

# Multiple attachments - return list
chart1 = create_chart(data1)  # Returns dict
chart2 = create_chart(data2)  # Returns dict
[chart1, chart2]  # Both dicts visible to LLM

# Functional composition (recommended for data viz)
chart = create_vega_chart(
    spec=spec,
    data_attachments=[jq_query(source, '.[] | select(.value > 10)')]
)
chart  # Returns attachment dict
```

**Example Scripts:**

1. Simple note creation:
```python
result = add_or_update_note(
    title='Meeting Notes',
    content='Discussed project timeline'
)
print('Created note:', result)
```

2. Conditional logic with search:
```python
def process_todos():
    notes = search_notes(query='TODO')
    
    if len(notes) > 0:
        print('Found', len(notes), 'TODO items')
        for note in notes:
            print('-', note['title'])
    else:
        print('No TODO items found')
    return notes

# Call the function
process_todos()
```

3. Complex automation:
```python
def create_project_summary():
    # Search for notes, create summary, send email
    project_notes = search_notes(query='Project Alpha')
    
    summary = 'Project Alpha Summary:\n\n'
    for note in project_notes:
        summary += '- ' + note['title'] + '\n'
    
    if len(project_notes) > 0:
        add_or_update_note(
            title='Project Alpha Summary',
            content=summary
        )
        result = send_email(
            to='team@example.com',
            subject='Weekly Project Summary',
            body=summary
        )
        return {'notes_found': len(project_notes), 'email_result': result}
    else:
        return {'notes_found': 0, 'email_result': 'No notes to summarize'}

# Execute the function
create_project_summary()
```

4. Working with user attachments (attachment ID provided by LLM):
```python
# Attachment ID passed to script by LLM based on conversation context
# Example: LLM calls execute_script with attachment_id parameter
def process_user_attachment(attachment_id):
    # Get attachment details
    attachment_info = attachment_get(attachment_id)
    
    if attachment_info:
        print('Processing:', attachment_info['description'])
        
        # Process the attachment with a tool (ID auto-converted to content)
        if 'image' in attachment_info['mime_type']:
            analysis = tools_execute('analyze_image', image_data=attachment_id)
            # Send results back to user via LLM tools
            wake_llm({'message': 'Analysis: ' + analysis, 'attachments': [attachment_id]})
        else:
            # Use attach_to_response LLM tool to send attachment back
            tools_execute('attach_to_response', attachment_ids=[attachment_id])
    else:
        print('Attachment not found or not accessible')

# Call with attachment ID from LLM context
# process_user_attachment('uuid-from-llm-context')
```

5. Data visualization with automatic attachment propagation:
```python
# Create a chart - attachment automatically returns to LLM
spec = {
  '$schema': 'https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json',
  'data': {'name': 'sensor_data'},
  'mark': 'line',
  'encoding': {
    'x': {'field': 'timestamp', 'type': 'temporal'},
    'y': {'field': 'temperature', 'type': 'quantitative'}
  }
}

# Chart is automatically visible - no need for attach_to_response!
create_vega_chart(
  spec=json_encode(spec),
  data_attachments=[sensor_attachment_id],
  title='Temperature Over Time'
)
```

6. Multi-chart dashboard:
```python
# Create multiple related charts
temp_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'line', ...}
humidity_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'area', ...}

temp_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(temp_spec), data_attachments=[data])
humidity_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(humidity_spec), data_attachments=[data])

# Both charts automatically visible to LLM
[temp_chart, humidity_chart]
```
functionDeclarations.name: execute_script

script.description:
The Python script code to execute (inline mode). Omit this and use 'name' instead to run a stored script.

The script can:
• Define variables and functions
• Use control flow (if/else, for loops)
• Call any available Family Assistant tool
• Process and transform data
• Print output for debugging
• Return a value (the last expression is returned)

Scripts should be self-contained and handle errors gracefully.

**Wake LLM Contexts:**
If the script calls wake_llm(), the contexts will be included in the response.
This allows the LLM to receive and process wake requests from scripts.

**Return Values:**
Returns a string containing the script execution result:
• Anything printed with print() appears first under a '--- Script Output ---' section
• On success with return value: 'Script result: [value]' or for dict/list: 'Script result:\n[JSON formatted]'
• On success without return: 'Script executed successfully with no return value.'
• If wake_llm() called: Also includes '--- Wake LLM Contexts ---' section with context details
• On error: any output printed before the failure is included above the error message
• On syntax error: 'Error: Syntax error in script [at line N]: [details]'
• On timeout: 'Error: Script execution timed out after [N] seconds'
• On execution error: 'Error: Script execution failed: [details]'
• On unexpected error: 'Error: Unexpected error executing script: [details]'

globals.description:
Optional dictionary of global variables to inject into the script.

These variables will be available in the script's global scope.
Useful for passing configuration, data, or context to the script.

Example:
{
  "user_email": "john@example.com",
  "project_id": 123,
  "tags": ["important", "urgent"]
}

These can then be used in the script as regular variables.

name.description:
Name of a stored script to execute (alternative to inline 'script').
Use list_scripts to see available stored scripts. When using 'name',
pass arguments via 'parameters' instead of 'globals'.

parameters.description:
Parameters to pass to a stored script as global variables.
Only used with 'name'. Validated against the script's parameter schema if defined.

            analysis = tools_execute('analyze_image', image_data=attachment_id)
            # Send results back to user via LLM tools
            wake_llm({'message': 'Analysis: ' + analysis, 'attachments': [attachment_id]})
        else:
            # Use attach_to_response LLM tool to send attachment back
            tools_execute('attach_to_response', attachment_ids=[attachment_id])
    else:
        print('Attachment not found or not accessible')

# Call with attachment ID from LLM context
# process_user_attachment('uuid-from-llm-context')
```

5. Data visualization with automatic attachment propagation:
```python
# Create a chart - attachment automatically returns to LLM
spec = {
  '$schema': 'https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json',
  'data': {'name': 'sensor_data'},
  'mark': 'line',
  'encoding': {
    'x': {'field': 'timestamp', 'type': 'temporal'},
    'y': {'field': 'temperature', 'type': 'quantitative'}
  }
}

# Chart is automatically visible - no need for attach_to_response!
create_vega_chart(
  spec=json_encode(spec),
  data_attachments=[sensor_attachment_id],
  title='Temperature Over Time'
)
```

6. Multi-chart dashboard:
```python
# Create multiple related charts
temp_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'line', ...}
humidity_spec = {'$schema': '...', 'mark': 'area', ...}

temp_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(temp_spec), data_attachments=[data])
humidity_chart = create_vega_chart(spec=json_encode(humidity_spec), data_attachments=[data])

# Both charts automatically visible to LLM
[temp_chart, humidity_chart]
```
functionDeclarations.name: execute_script

script.description:
The Python script code to execute (inline mode). Omit this and use 'name' instead to run a stored script.

The script can:
• Define variables and functions
• Use control flow (if/else, for loops)
• Call any available Family Assistant tool
• Process and transform data
• Print output for debugging
• Return a value (the last expression is returned)

Scripts should be self-contained and handle errors gracefully.

**Wake LLM Contexts:**
If the script calls wake_llm(), the contexts will be included in the response.
This allows the LLM to receive and process wake requests from scripts.

**Return Values:**
Returns a string containing the script execution result:
• Anything printed with print() appears first under a '--- Script Output ---' section
• On success with return value: 'Script result: [value]' or for dict/list: 'Script result:\n[JSON formatted]'
• On success without return: 'Script executed successfully with no return value.'
• If wake_llm() called: Also includes '--- Wake LLM Contexts ---' section with context details
• On error: any output printed before the failure is included above the error message
• On syntax error: 'Error: Syntax error in script [at line N]: [details]'
• On timeout: 'Error: Script execution timed out after [N] seconds'
• On execution error: 'Error: Script execution failed: [details]'
• On unexpected error: 'Error: Unexpected error executing script: [details]'

globals.description:
Optional dictionary of global variables to inject into the script.

These variables will be available in the script's global scope.
Useful for passing configuration, data, or context to the script.

Example:
{
  "user_email": "john@example.com",
  "project_id": 123,
  "tags": ["important", "urgent"]
}

These can then be used in the script as regular variables.

name.description:
Name of a stored script to execute (alternative to inline 'script').
Use list_scripts to see available stored scripts. When using 'name',
pass arguments via 'parameters' instead of 'globals'.

parameters.description:
Parameters to pass to a stored script as global variables.
Only used with 'name'. Validated against the script's parameter schema if defined.
